subject: Production latency spike — remediation & commercial path
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fabled.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Green <marcus.green@fabled.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — immediate attention requested

Jordan / Ben —

We started seeing end-user degradation at ~08:45 PDT this morning. Symptoms across multiple regions: increased P99 latency (up ~3.2x), request-level error rate rising to 4.8% on our top API route, and sustained throughput backpressure from our ingest pipeline. This is impacting live customers (several on web sessions dropped) and our first-tier ops are fielding ~15 tickets/min.

Can you confirm:
- Whether this is an infra-side regression or a model-serving/backpressure event?
- ETA for a remediation window / rollback if you identify a risky rollout?
- A preliminary ballpark for commercial remediation (credits) we should expect if this is a verified SLA breach?

Attached: a short incident timeline we compiled so far (incident_timeline.pdf). We need a formal statement for our execs and procurement asap — Marcus and I will escalate internally if we don't get a clear remediation plan within 4 hours.

Thanks — this is high priority.

Elena Ruiz
VP Engineering, Fabled AI
elena.ruiz@fabled.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fabled.ai>, Marcus Green <marcus.green@fabled.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — immediate attention requested

Elena / Marcus —

First, I’m sorry — and thank you for the rapid heads-up and the timeline. Ben and I are standing up a war room now (invites sent). Initial notes: our telemetry is showing an unusual tokenization cache pressure in the east region coincident with a canary model rollout at 08:30 PDT. We are rolling the canary back as a precaution and will throttle incoming new sessions to prevent further customer impact while we stabilize.

Immediate asks for your team:
- Can you share the list of top 5 customers impacted (names & estimated revenue impact) so we can prioritize?
- Any customer-initiated mitigations already in place (client-side retries, reduced concurrency)?

We’ll get a preliminary root-cause hypothesis and a remediation ETA in the next 90 minutes. For commercial remediation, I’ll work with Marissa and Finance to produce a provisional credit estimate and a formal offer. Will follow up in the war room.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace OConnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Fabled AI — credit calc & rollback plan (draft)

Team —

War room summary (top-line):
- Canary model rollout at 08:30 PDT -> token cache pressure -> elevated latencies & client retries -> visible error spike at 08:45. Canary rollback initiated at 09:20; error rate began to return to baseline by ~09:55.
- Impact window: 08:45–09:55 PDT (~70 minutes). Peak affected requests estimated at 47k/min.

Commercial / customer-facing approach (draft):
1) Offer an immediate one-time credit pegged to the verified impact window. Proposal: credit equal to 10% of net hosting charges for impacted accounts for the month of June (or a minimum credit of $25k for enterprise). Rationale: aligns with observed severity and keeps negotiations straightforward.
2) Technical remediation: documented rollback + short-term throttling rulebook; follow-up post-mortem by EOD Tuesday.
3) Operational remediation: canary gating + automated cache warming for subsequent rollouts.

Open items I need from you before I send a formal offer to Fabled:
- Ben: quick verification of the usage/ingest numbers and per-account chargebacks (attach q2_credit_calc.xlsx).
- Grace: confirm SLA formula to apply (P99 + error rate threshold) and any binding contractual caps.
- Dylan: timeline & short post-mortem draft.
- Marissa: sign-off on commercial language and whether Finance will accept 10% / $25k floor.

I’ve attached a working spreadsheet (q2_credit_calc.xlsx) with a baseline calculation you can edit. I’ll hold external communication until we have firm numbers.

—Jordan
From: Marcus Green <marcus.green@fabled.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fabled.ai>
Cc: procurement@fabled.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — remediation & commercial path

Jordan —

Thanks for the update and the war room earlier. Fabled needs a formal remediation proposal that includes:
- Exact credit calculation & how it maps to the contract SLA clauses (section 4.2).
- A commitment timeline for the rollout gates and automated cache warming.
- Exec-level sign-off from Redwood (we will reciprocate).

Procurement has asked that any commercial remediation be presented as a one-page Amendment for signature; they can accept DocuSign. Please include a final figure and the associated breakdown (per-customer, total).

We are scheduling an internal leadership sync tomorrow; please aim to have a draft Amendment + calculation emailed to procurement@fabled.ai before 09:00 PDT on Thu 17 Jun. If you can’t meet that, let me know and we will escalate.

Regards,
Marcus Green
Head of Platform Ops, Fabled AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fabled.ai>, Marcus Green <marcus.green@fabled.ai>, procurement@fabled.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace OConnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Formal offer: verified credit + remediation commitments

Elena / Marcus / procurement —

Appreciate the patience while we completed the verification. Attached are the two items you asked for: (1) q2_credit_calc.xlsx — the per-customer verified impact and the resulting credit figures, and (2) a one-page Amendment draft prepared for DocuSign. Links attached: https://app.docusign.com/prepare?envelopeId=ABC123 (Amendment draft).

Summary of the offer (final):
- Verified impact window: 2027-06-14T08:45–09:55 PDT per our telemetry.
- Calculated remediation: a one-time credit equal to 11% of June hosting charges for impacted customers, with a $22,500 minimum credit per enterprise account (we adjusted from the draft after Finance review). Total aggregate credit across affected customers: $198,700.
- Technical commitments: mandatory canary gating for all model rollouts for 30 days; automated KV-cache warmup for first-stage canaries; a runbook for throttling that will be published in the Console by Monday EOD.
- Governance: Redwood exec sign-off provided by Marissa Cole (attached) and Jordan Blake (customer sponsor).

Next steps:
1) Procurement: please review the Amendment and open the DocuSign routing (link above).
2) We will hold an executive touchpoint on Mon 21 Jun 09:00 PDT (invite sent) to close commercial acceptance and the technical remediation timeline.
3) Post-mortem: public-facing post-mortem will be delivered within 5 business days after Monday’s touchpoint.

If you need different figures or a structured payment schedule instead of a lump-sum credit, we can adjust — please give a clear preference in your response.

Apologies again for the disruption, and thank you for working through this with us.

—Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: q2_credit_calc.xlsx, incident_timeline.pdf
